questions.question: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.explanation: Work is measured in Joules (J). 1 Joule of work is done when a force of 1 N moves an object through 1 m in the direction of the force.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Energy, like work, is measured in Joules (J), since energy is the capacity to do work.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is measured in Watts (W). 1 Watt equals 1 Joule of work done per second (1 W = 1 J/s).

questions.question: What is the formula for work done by a constant force?
questions.explanation: Work done = Force × displacement in the direction of the force, W = Fs (more precisely W = Fs cos θ).

questions.question: What is the formula for kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. KE = 1/2 mv², where m is mass and v is velocity.

questions.question: What is the formula for gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy depends on mass (m), gravitational acceleration (g), and height (h): PE = mgh.

questions.question: What is the formula for power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work: P = Work done ÷ Time taken (P = W/t).

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of energy?
questions.explanation: Heat (thermal energy) is a form of energy. Force, mass, and displacement are not forms of energy themselves.

questions.question: What is the definition of energy?
options: The force applied to an object
questions.explanation: Energy is defined as the capacity or ability of a body to do work.

questions.question: What does the law of conservation of energy state?
options: Energy can be created but not destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed
questions.correct_answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that total energy in an isolated system remains constant; energy only changes from one form to another.

questions.question: What is mechanical energy?
options: The sum of kinetic and potential energy
questions.correct_answer: The sum of kinetic and potential energy
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy of a body is the sum of its kinetic energy (energy of motion) and potential energy (energy of position).

questions.question: What condition must be met for work to be done on an object?
options: A force must act and cause displacement
The object must move at constant speed
The object must be lifted upward
questions.correct_answer: A force must act and cause displacement
questions.explanation: Work is done only when a force acts on an object and causes it to be displaced in the direction of the force.

questions.question: When is work done said to be zero?
options: When force and displacement are in the same direction
When there is no displacement, or force and displacement are perpendicular
When the object moves very fast
When the force is very large
questions.correct_answer: When there is no displacement, or force and displacement are perpendicular
questions.explanation: Work is zero if there is no displacement, or if the force is perpendicular to the displacement (cos 90° = 0).

questions.question: What is 1 Watt equal to?
questions.explanation: 1 Watt is defined as 1 Joule of work done per second: 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.question: Which quantity represents the capacity of a body to do work due to its motion?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body because of its motion.

questions.question: Which quantity represents the energy stored in a body due to its position or state?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is the stored energy a body has because of its position (e.g., height) or state (e.g., a stretched spring).

questions.question: What is the larger practical unit of power commonly used for engines, equal to 746 W?
questions.explanation: Horsepower (hp) is a practical unit of power; 1 horsepower = 746 Watts, often used to rate engines and motors.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable because it is continuously replenished by the sun. Coal, natural gas, and petroleum are non-renewable fossil fuels.

questions.question: What type of energy is stored in a stretched or compressed spring?
questions.explanation: A stretched or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy due to the deformation of its shape.

questions.question: Which unit is commonly used by electricity companies to measure electrical energy consumption?
questions.explanation: Electrical energy consumption is commonly measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), a larger practical unit of energy used on electricity bills.

questions.question: What is efficiency of a machine?
options: The ratio of input energy to output energy
The ratio of useful output energy to input energy, expressed as a percentage
The total energy supplied to a machine
The speed at which a machine operates
questions.correct_answer: The ratio of useful output energy to input energy, expressed as a percentage
questions.explanation: Efficiency = (Useful output energy / Total input energy) × 100%. It shows how effectively a machine converts input energy into useful work.

questions.question: Which form of energy is produced by the movement of electric charge?
questions.explanation: Electrical energy is associated with the flow (movement) of electric charge, such as current through a conductor.

questions.question: What quantity does the area under a force-displacement graph represent?
questions.explanation: The area under a force-displacement graph equals the work done, since work = force × displacement.

questions.question: When a body falls freely under gravity, what happens to its potential energy?
questions.explanation: As a body falls, its height above the ground decreases, so its gravitational potential energy (PE = mgh) decreases.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes non-renewable energy sources?
options: Sources that replenish naturally and quickly
Sources that are limited and take millions of years to form
Sources that come only from sunlight
questions.correct_answer: Sources that are limited and take millions of years to form
questions.explanation: Non-renewable energy sources, such as coal, oil, and natural gas, exist in limited quantities and take millions of years to form naturally.

questions.question: A boy pushes a wall with all his strength but the wall does not move. How much work is done on the wall?
questions.explanation: Since there is no displacement of the wall, the work done is zero, regardless of how much force is applied.

questions.question: A coolie carries a load on his head and walks horizontally. What is the work done against gravity?
options: Maximum, since the load is heavy
Zero, because displacement is perpendicular to the gravitational force
Negative, because he is walking forward
Equal to the force times the horizontal distance
questions.correct_answer: Zero, because displacement is perpendicular to the gravitational force
questions.explanation: The gravitational force acts vertically downward while the displacement is horizontal, so the angle between them is 90°, making the work done against gravity zero.

questions.question: A ball is thrown straight up. At the highest point of its path, what is its kinetic energy?
options: Equal to its potential energy at the ground
questions.explanation: At the highest point, the ball's velocity momentarily becomes zero, so its kinetic energy (KE = 1/2 mv²) is also zero.

questions.question: A pendulum bob swings from one extreme position to the mean position. What happens to its energy?
options: Kinetic energy converts to potential energy
Potential energy converts to kinetic energy
questions.correct_answer: Potential energy converts to kinetic energy
questions.explanation: As the bob moves from the extreme (highest) position to the mean (lowest) position, its height decreases and speed increases, so potential energy converts into kinetic energy.

questions.question: Two objects of equal mass are dropped from the same height. Which one has greater potential energy just before release?
options: The one with more surface area
questions.explanation: Since PE = mgh depends only on mass, gravitational acceleration, and height, equal mass and equal height mean equal potential energy for both objects.

questions.question: A crane lifts a load slowly and another crane lifts an identical load quickly to the same height. Which crane does more work?
options: Both do the same amount of work
questions.correct_answer: Both do the same amount of work
questions.explanation: Work done depends on force and displacement, not on time. Since both loads are lifted the same height, the work done is the same; only the power differs.

questions.question: In the previous scenario, which crane delivers more power?
questions.explanation: Power = Work/time. Since the faster crane does the same work in less time, it delivers greater power.

questions.question: A car engine and a bicycle both do the same amount of work climbing a hill, but the car does it in less time. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: Since power is work divided by time, doing the same work in a shorter time means the car develops greater power than the bicycle.

questions.question: A stretched bow is about to release an arrow. What type of energy is stored in the bow just before release?
questions.explanation: The bent bow is deformed from its natural shape, storing elastic potential energy, which converts to kinetic energy of the arrow upon release.

questions.question: A book rests on a table. Why is no work being done on the book by gravity, even though gravity acts on it?
options: Because the book has no mass
Because there is no displacement of the book
questions.correct_answer: Because there is no displacement of the book
questions.explanation: Work requires displacement. Since the book is stationary, there is no displacement, so the work done by gravity on it is zero.

questions.question: A ball rolling on a frictionless horizontal surface has no change in height. What happens to its mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: With no friction and no change in height, there is no energy loss or gain, so kinetic energy stays constant and total mechanical energy is conserved.

questions.question: A moving car brakes and comes to a stop due to friction. What happens to its kinetic energy?
options: It is transformed mainly into heat energy
It converts entirely into potential energy
questions.correct_answer: It is transformed mainly into heat energy
questions.explanation: Friction between the brakes and wheels converts the car's kinetic energy mainly into heat (and some sound) energy, causing the car to slow down and stop.

questions.question: Why does a solar panel represent an example of a renewable energy source?
options: Because it stores fossil fuel energy
Because sunlight is continuously available and does not get used up
Because it produces electricity without any energy input
Because it converts chemical energy directly to work
questions.correct_answer: Because sunlight is continuously available and does not get used up
questions.explanation: Solar energy comes from sunlight, which is continuously replenished and will not run out on a human timescale, making it a renewable source.

questions.question: A machine has an efficiency of less than 100%. What does this indicate?
options: The machine produces more energy than it receives
Some input energy is lost, often as heat, rather than converted to useful output
The machine violates the law of conservation of energy
The machine does no useful work at all
questions.correct_answer: Some input energy is lost, often as heat, rather than converted to useful output
questions.explanation: No real machine is 100% efficient because some input energy is always lost to friction, heat, or sound rather than being converted into useful output work.

questions.question: A weightlifter holds a barbell stationary above his head for 30 seconds. How much work is he doing on the barbell during this time?
options: A large amount, since he is exerting great force
Work equal to the barbell's weight times the height it was lifted
Zero, because there is no displacement while holding it
Negative work, because he is getting tired
questions.correct_answer: Zero, because there is no displacement while holding it
questions.explanation: Work requires displacement. While the barbell is held stationary, there is no displacement, so no work is done on it during that period, even though force is being exerted.

questions.question: A skier slides down a snowy slope from rest. As she descends, what happens to her potential and kinetic energy (ignoring friction)?
options: Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases
Potential energy increases while kinetic energy decreases
questions.correct_answer: Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases
questions.explanation: As height decreases while sliding down, potential energy decreases, and this lost potential energy converts into kinetic energy, so kinetic energy increases.

questions.question: Which requires more power: lifting a 10 kg box to a height of 2 m in 5 seconds, or lifting the same box to the same height in 10 seconds?
options: Power cannot be determined without force values
questions.explanation: The work done is the same in both cases, but doing it in less time (5 s) means greater power, since power is inversely proportional to time for the same work.

questions.question: A person pushes a stalled car but it does not move because static friction is too strong. Is any work done on the car?
options: No, because there is no displacement
Yes, but only a small amount
It depends on how hard the person pushes
questions.correct_answer: No, because there is no displacement
questions.explanation: Since the car does not move, there is no displacement, and therefore no work is done on it, regardless of the effort or force applied.

questions.question: Why is coal considered a poor long-term energy choice compared to solar energy?
options: Coal produces more energy per kilogram than the sun
Coal is a non-renewable resource that will eventually be exhausted
Coal is more expensive to extract than solar panels
Coal cannot be used to generate electricity
questions.correct_answer: Coal is a non-renewable resource that will eventually be exhausted
questions.explanation: Coal takes millions of years to form and exists in limited supply, so continued use will eventually exhaust it, unlike the continuously available solar energy.

questions.question: In a hydroelectric power plant, water stored at height falls and turns a turbine. What energy transformation occurs?
options: Potential energy to kinetic energy to electrical energy
questions.correct_answer: Potential energy to kinetic energy to electrical energy
questions.explanation: Stored water has gravitational potential energy; as it falls, this converts to kinetic energy, which then turns turbines to generate electrical energy.

questions.question: Two students of equal mass run up the same staircase; Student A takes 10 seconds and Student B takes 15 seconds. Who does more work, and who has more power?
options: A does more work; B has more power
Both do the same work; A has more power
B does more work; A has more power
Both do the same work and have the same power
questions.correct_answer: Both do the same work; A has more power
questions.explanation: Both students rise through the same height and have equal mass, so work done (W = mgh) is the same. Since A takes less time, A has more power.

questions.question: Why does a burning candle represent a transformation of energy?
options: It converts electrical energy into potential energy
It converts chemical energy stored in wax into heat and light energy
It converts kinetic energy into chemical energy
It creates new energy that did not exist before
questions.correct_answer: It converts chemical energy stored in wax into heat and light energy
questions.explanation: The wax stores chemical energy, which is released as heat and light energy during combustion — an example of energy transformation, not creation.

questions.question: A cyclist pedals uphill at constant speed. Why does she feel like she is doing more work than cycling on a flat road at the same speed?
options: Because her kinetic energy is increasing
Because she is also gaining potential energy by increasing height
Because her mass increases going uphill
questions.correct_answer: Because she is also gaining potential energy by increasing height
questions.explanation: On a hill, in addition to overcoming friction and air resistance, she must also do extra work to increase her gravitational potential energy as her height increases.

questions.question: An electric heater converts electrical energy into heat energy with very little loss. What does this suggest about its efficiency?
options: It has high efficiency, close to 100%
It violates the law of conservation of energy
Efficiency does not apply to heaters
questions.correct_answer: It has high efficiency, close to 100%
questions.explanation: Since nearly all the input electrical energy is converted into useful heat output with minimal loss, the heater's efficiency is high, close to 100%.

questions.question: A satellite orbits the Earth at a constant height and constant speed. What can be said about its total mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: Since both the height (potential energy) and speed (kinetic energy) of the satellite remain constant in a stable circular orbit, its total mechanical energy stays constant.
